title: The last even loss in Prime Nim
words: In Prime Nim almost every losing pile size is odd. The only even ones found are 0, 10, 34, 100 and 310. Prove there are no more.
math: For the subtraction game with prime moves, prove $\{n \text{ even}: G(n)=0\}=\{0,10,34,100,310\}$.

title: The 3p+4 seven-cycle
words: Send a prime p to the largest prime factor of 3p + 4. Every prime tested ends in the loop 11 → 37 → 23 → 73 → 223 → 673 → 17 → 11. Prove all do.
math: Prove every orbit of $p\mapsto P(3p+4)$ on primes enters the cycle $(11,37,23,73,223,673,17)$.

title: The 5p+4 nine-cycle
words: For p ↦ largest prime factor of 5p + 4, every tested prime ends in one loop of nine primes through 11. Prove all do.
math: Prove every orbit of $p\mapsto P(5p+4)$ on primes enters the cycle $(11,59,23,17,89,449,173,79,19)$.

title: Escaping p²+p+1
words: Start at 2 and repeatedly take the largest prime factor of p² + p + 1. Show the sequence grows without bound.
math: Prove the orbit of $2$ under $p\mapsto P(p^2+p+1)$ is unbounded.

title: Exponential growth of square-plus-one orbits
words: Show square-plus-one sequences, when they don't loop, grow at a steady exponential rate in the number of digits.
math: Prove that for almost every $n$ (density 1), $\lim_{k}\frac1k\log\log Q^k(n)$ exists and equals a constant $\gamma>0$; identify $\gamma$.

title: Recursive basins of square-plus-one
words: Is there an algorithm that decides, for any n, whether its square-plus-one sequence ever hits 5?
math: Decide whether $\{n:\exists k\ Q^k(n)=5\}$ is a recursive set, where $Q(n)=P(n^2+1)$.

title: Irrational orbit sum
words: Add the reciprocals of the square-plus-one sequence starting from 2. Show the total is irrational.
math: Prove $\sum_{k\ge0}1/Q^k(2)$ converges and is irrational.

title: Largest factor of n²+1 mod 8
words: The largest prime factor of n² + 1 is always 1 or 5 mod 8 (or 2). Show both happen equally often.
math: Prove $\#\{n\le x: P(n^2+1)\equiv1\ (8)\}\sim\#\{n\le x:P(n^2+1)\equiv5\ (8)\}\sim x/2$.

title: Largest factor of shifted primes mod 4
words: For primes p, look at the largest prime factor of p − 1. Show it is 1 mod 4 exactly half the time.
math: Prove $\#\{p\le x: P(p-1)\equiv1\ (4)\}\sim\tfrac12\pi(x)$.

title: Hat percolation is conformally invariant
words: Show critical percolation on the hat tiling's tiles has crossing probabilities given by Cardy's formula.
math: For critical site percolation on hat tiles, prove crossing probabilities of conformal rectangles converge to Cardy's formula as the mesh $\to0$.

title: Critical Ising on the hat is SLE(3)
words: Show the interface in the critical Ising model on a hat tiling converges to the random curve SLE(3), even though the graph is not isoradial.
math: For the critical Ising model on the hat graph with Dobrushin boundary conditions, prove the interface converges to chordal SLE$_3$.

title: Hat packing density is irrational
words: The densest packing of hats without reflections leaves gaps. Show the best density is an irrational number.
math: Prove the maximal packing density of congruent hats under orientation-preserving isometries is irrational.

title: Lorenz dimension is irrational
words: Show the Hausdorff dimension of the classic Lorenz attractor is irrational.
math: For $\sigma=10,\beta=8/3,\rho=28$, prove $\dim_H(\mathcal{A})\notin\mathbb{Q}$.

title: Hat Neumann eigenvalue is transcendental
words: Show the first nonzero frequency of an insulated hat-shaped membrane is transcendental.
math: Prove the first nonzero Neumann eigenvalue $\mu_2$ of the hat polygon (unit kite side) is transcendental.

title: Simple spectrum of the hat
words: Show no two vibration frequencies of the hat-shaped drum coincide.
math: Prove every Dirichlet eigenvalue of the hat polygon is simple.

title: Conformal radius of the hat
words: Map a disc conformally onto the hat so the centre goes to the hat's centroid. Show the scale factor is transcendental.
math: Prove the conformal radius of the hat polygon at its centroid is transcendental.

title: Spanning trees inside the prime-sum graph
words: Show every balanced tree of bounded degree on 2n vertices can be laid out on 1 to 2n so all its edges sum to primes.
math: Prove that for every $\Delta$ there is $n_0$ such that every tree on $2n\ge n_0$ vertices with maximum degree $\le\Delta$ and bipartition classes of size $n$ is a spanning subgraph of the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$.

title: Spanning trees inside the square-sum graph
words: Show every tree of maximum degree 3 on N vertices fits inside the square-sum graph on 1 to N.
math: Prove every tree on $N\ge N_0$ vertices with maximum degree $\le3$ is a spanning subgraph of $S_N$.

title: Triangle factors of square sums
words: Split 1 to N into triples so that within each triple all three pairwise sums are perfect squares.
math: Prove $S_N$ has a $K_3$-factor for all sufficiently large $N\equiv0\pmod 3$.

title: AKLT on the hat
words: Show the AKLT quantum spin model placed on a hat tiling has an energy gap above its ground state.
math: For the AKLT Hamiltonian on the vertex graph of a hat tiling (spin $d(v)/2$ at vertex $v$), prove a uniform spectral gap on finite patches.

title: Node Kayles on square sums
words: Players alternately pick an unused number up to N that does not sum to a square with any picked number. Last to move wins. Decide the winner for large N.
math: Determine the outcome of Node Kayles on $S_N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

title: Square-sum ordering with bounded displacement
words: Order all positive integers so neighbours always sum to squares, and no number moves more than a fixed distance from its natural place.
math: Decide whether there is a bijection $\pi:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $\pi(i)+\pi(i+1)$ always a square and $\sup_i|\pi(i)-i|/\sqrt i<\infty$.

title: Digit-restricted Liouville
words: Show the Liouville function has no bias on seven-free numbers in short intervals.
math: Prove $\sum_{x<n\le x+H,\ 7\notin n}\lambda(n)=o(\#\{x<n\le x+H:7\notin n\})$ for almost all $x\le X$ whenever $H\to\infty$.

title: Square-plus-one orbits avoid small primes
words: Show that infinitely many starting numbers have square-plus-one sequences that never fall below their start.
math: Prove infinitely many $n$ with $Q^k(n)\ge n$ for all $k\ge1$.

title: Prime cycles of all lengths
words: Show that for every length L, some map p ↦ largest prime factor of ap + b has a loop of exactly length L.
math: Prove that for every $L\ge1$ there are $a,b\ge1$ such that $p\mapsto P(ap+b)$ has a periodic orbit of exact length $L$.

title: Hat SAW connective constant is irrational
words: Show the growth constant of self-avoiding walks on the hat tiling's neighbour graph is irrational.
math: Prove the connective constant of the hat adjacency graph is irrational.

title: Critical hat Ising temperature is irrational
words: Show the critical temperature of the Ising model on a hat tiling is not a rational multiple of the coupling.
math: Prove $\beta_c J\notin\mathbb{Q}$ for the ferromagnetic Ising model on the hat graph.

title: Spectre hard hexagons
words: Show the hard-core gas on the spectre tiling has exactly one phase transition, at a single sharp activity.
math: Prove the hard-core model on the spectre adjacency graph has a unique critical activity $\lambda_c$ with uniqueness for $\lambda<\lambda_c$ and non-uniqueness for $\lambda>\lambda_c$.

title: The 7p+4 funnel, almost always
words: Show almost every prime eventually falls into the 12-cycle of the 7p + 4 map.
math: Prove the primes whose $p\mapsto P(7p+4)$ orbit enters its 12-cycle have relative density 1.

title: Largest factor ratio of consecutive primes
words: For consecutive primes p < q, compare the largest prime factors of p − 1 and q − 1. Show each is larger half the time.

title: Seven-free primes in Piatetski-Shapiro sequences
words: Show infinitely many primes of the form ⌊n^1.1⌋ have no digit 7.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $\lfloor n^{1.1}\rfloor$ free of the decimal digit 7.

title: Square-sum Ramsey with many colours
words: Colour 1 to N with r colours. Show some colour contains four numbers whose six pairwise sums are all squares, once N is large enough.
math: Prove that for every $r$ there is $N$ such that every $r$-colouring of $[N]$ has a monochromatic $K_4$ in $S_N$, or show it fails for some $r$.

title: Square-sum independence in short intervals
words: Find the largest set of numbers in [x, x + y] with no two summing to a square, for y about the square root of x.
math: For $y=\lfloor\sqrt x\rfloor$, determine $\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac1y\max\{|A|:A\subseteq[x,x+y],\ a+a'\ne\square\}$.

title: The 4p+1 map is not periodic mod 3
words: Show the order in which primes enter the 4p + 1 loop is not governed by any simple congruence.
math: Prove there is no modulus $M$ such that the entry point of $p$ into the 8-cycle of $p\mapsto P(4p+1)$ depends only on $p\bmod M$.

title: Hat Hofstadter gaps all open
words: Show every gap predicted by the gap-labelling theorem actually opens in the hat tiling's electronic spectrum.
math: Prove the dry ten-Martini property for the vertex adjacency operator of the hat tiling: every gap label in the $K_0$-group of the hull corresponds to an open gap.

title: Hat billiard Veech property
words: Billiards in the hat polygon unfolds to a translation surface. Decide whether it has the rare Veech property.
math: Decide whether the translation surface obtained by unfolding billiards in the hat polygon is a Veech surface.

title: Gerver sofa eigenvalue is transcendental
words: Show the lowest vibration frequency of a drum shaped like Gerver's sofa is transcendental.
math: Prove the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of Gerver's sofa is transcendental.

title: Quasi-independence of square-plus-one steps
words: Show the largest prime factors of n² + 1 and (n + 1)² + 1 are nearly independent in size.

title: Prime Nim on Gaussian integers
words: Play Prime Nim with Gaussian integers: subtract a Gaussian prime staying in the first quadrant. Show losing positions have density zero.
math: For positions $a+bi$ with $a,b\ge0$ and moves $z\mapsto z-\pi$ with $\pi$ a Gaussian prime and the result in the closed first quadrant, prove the P-positions have density 0.

title: Prime Nim's mod-3 bias
words: Losing pile sizes in Prime Nim are about three times as likely to be 1 mod 3 as 0 mod 3. Find the exact limiting proportions.
math: For the prime subtraction game, prove the limits $\lim_x\#\{n\le x:G(n)=0,\ n\equiv r\ (3)\}/\#\{n\le x:G(n)=0\}$ exist for $r=0,1,2$, and determine them.

title: Square losses in Prime Nim
words: Many perfect squares (1, 9, 25, 49, 100, 121, …) are losing Prime Nim positions. Show there are infinitely many.
math: Prove infinitely many perfect squares $k^2$ satisfy $G(k^2)=0$ in the prime subtraction game.

title: Progressions of Prime Nim losses
words: Show the losing positions of Prime Nim contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions.
math: Prove $\{n:G(n)=0\}$ contains $k$-term arithmetic progressions for every $k$.

title: Cube-sum triangle factors
words: Split 1 to N into triples so that within each triple all three pairwise sums are perfect cubes.
math: Prove $C_N$ has a $K_3$-factor for all sufficiently large $N\equiv0\pmod3$, or show it fails for infinitely many such $N$.

title: Bombieri–Vinogradov for seven-free primes in base 10
words: Show seven-free primes are well distributed in arithmetic progressions on average over moduli up to x^θ, for some θ > 0, in base 10.
math: Prove there is $\theta>0$ such that $\sum_{q\le x^\theta}\max_{(a,q)=1}\big|\pi_7(x;q,a)-\frac{\pi_7(x)}{\varphi(q)}\big|\ll_A \pi_7(x)(\log x)^{-A}$, where $\pi_7$ counts 7-free primes (moduli coprime to 10).

title: Codes avoiding square distances
words: Find the largest set of binary strings of length n in which no two differ in a perfect-square number of positions. Find the exponential rate.
math: Let $A(n)$ be the largest $C\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ with $d_H(x,y)$ never a positive perfect square for $x\ne y\in C$. Determine $\lim_n\frac1n\log_2A(n)$.

title: Increasing square-plus-one factors
words: Among the largest prime factors of n² + 1 for n up to N, find the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
math: Determine $\theta$ with $L(N)=N^{\theta+o(1)}$, where $L(N)$ is the longest strictly increasing subsequence of $(P(n^2+1))_{n\le N}$.

title: Turning a hat by 60 degrees
words: Rotate a hat tile continuously by 60° inside a region of least possible area. Find that area.
math: Determine $\inf\{|E|: E\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ contains the trace of a continuous rigid motion carrying the unit hat to its rotation by $60^\circ$ about a point$\}$, and whether it is attained.

title: Density of Grundy value one in Prime Nim
words: Show the pile sizes with Grundy value exactly 1 in Prime Nim have a definite density, and that it is positive.
math: For the prime subtraction game, prove $\lim_x\frac1x\#\{n\le x:G(n)=1\}$ exists and is positive.
